neighbours.label: the word just before 'sales' in a business sales/marketing context (retail, property, venue, ticket ... sales)
fire: The quarterly report notes that online sales now exceed in-store retail sales for the chain.
Agents say that after the rate cut, residential property sales picked up across the suburbs.
The band earned more from merchandise sales at concerts than from streaming or album sales.
As head of marketing, she oversees the advertising budget and tracks weekly ticket sales.
The dealership's vice president said that used vehicle sales were up nine percent.
Compared with last year, the bakery's wholesale sales grew faster than its café sales.
The developer reported that condominium sales slowed sharply in the second quarter.
Industry analysts expect smartphone sales to recover once supply chains settle.
quiet: The quarterly report notes that the chain opened twelve new stores in the north.
Agents say that after the rate cut, more families started viewing homes in the suburbs.
The band earned praise for its concerts and for the new album's artwork.
As head of marketing, she oversees the advertising budget and the design team.
The dealership's vice president said that the service centre will move next spring.
Compared with last year, the bakery's wholesale bread looks and tastes better.
The developer reported that construction of the condominium tower was delayed.
Industry analysts expect smartphone screens to become cheaper next year.

notes: logit effect promotes ' sales'; isolated probes ('Retail sales fell') were weak (0.13), so this follows the card's longer business contexts
